doc.title: Marty Grosz interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995

title: Dreaming of playing in a dance band
summary: Seeing bands at New York theaters, he pictures himself in a mess jacket; a mess jacket is explained, and the comparison with kids wanting rock stardom today.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: That’s it. I thought immediately that these things always seem to happen with the onset of puberty. And they’re very much glandular in nature. And the, you know I saw myself, like the bands I went to see at the Paramount and the Strand and the Capitol Theaters in Manhattan, I saw myself — well, a mustache would be good, hair, there’s a lot of goo on the hair, slicked, you know, shiny, wearing one of those mess jackets.

A mess jacket is a jacket, you know, like the British officers wear, like formal wear, they wore them with striped tuxedo pants, and then the jacket was usually white. It was a summer jacket, and it only came down to here. And then you wore your miniature medals there, if you were British. But of course the musicians had those too. And I thought, oh,
to play in one of the bands, wow, you know. And I mean that was a great, great ambition in those days.
Almost like today, when a kid thinks of being in a heavy duty, you know, famous rock & roll band. Is that a fair statement? That this was—
